beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares an Archboard-only Codex home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. The owner lock and epoch ledger are the server's own. Then it starts the child and builds one generation's parts in the order they depend on each other.

beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: The server holds the link; a pane holds the lease
beats.body: The Archboard server's thread link names one workhorse, whichever pane speaks. The pane holding the lease sends its typed message straight to that thread as a turn or a steer, and edits the thread's queue. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations instead, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.heading: Voice is a separate thread, not a second mouth
beats.body: The coordinator is its own thread with its own model and settings, and the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorse and decides what the voice model says, and it runs only while voice is live. It does bounded work itself and routes anything sustained to the workhorse through the four operations.

beats.heading: The coordinator hears the workhorse at once
beats.body: While voice is live, a workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator, reaches the coordinator as one sentence in a turn/start: Codex adds it to the coordinator's running turn or starts one. beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares an Archboard-only Codex home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: Each tab holds its own link and lease

The pane that holds the tab's lease sends its typed message straight to that workhorse as a turn or a steer, and edits the thread's queue. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations instead, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.heading: Voice is a separate thread, not a second mouth
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares an Archboard-only Codex home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. The owner lock and epoch ledger are the server's own. Then it starts the child and builds one generation's parts in the order they depend on each other.

beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: Each tab holds its own link and lease
beats.body: Each browser tab is a tab session with its own thread link and its own lease. The tab's first message or Talk starts its conversation: the coordinator first, then the workhorse, which the link then names. The pane that holds the tab's lease sends its typed message straight to that workhorse as a turn or a steer, and edits the thread's queue. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations instead, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares an Archboard-only Codex home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. The owner lock and epoch ledger are the server's own. Then it starts the child and builds one generation's parts in the order they depend on each other.

beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: A tab holds one coordinator and a workhorse for each checkout
beats.body: Each browser tab is a tab session with its own lease and its own coordinator. A pane's first message or Talk starts its conversation: the coordinator first, then the workhorse of the checkout that pane shows, which that checkout's link then names. The pane that holds the lease sends its typed message straight to that workhorse as a turn or a steer, and edits that thread's queue. A pane that moves to another checkout reaches the workhorse there instead. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.heading: Voice is a separate thread that works in no checkout
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It runs in a directory of its own that holds no vault, so every command it runs names its checkout with -C. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorses and decides what the voice model says, and it runs only while voice is live. It does bounded work itself and routes anything sustained to the workhorse of the checkout it names, starting that workhorse when there is none. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The coordinator hears the workhorse at once
beats.body: While voice is live, a workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator, reaches the coordinator as one sentence in a turn/start: Codex adds it to the coordinator's running turn or starts one. With no voice session, or while a recording holds the voice, nothing is sent.

beats.heading: Board changes reach each workhorse quietly
beats.body: A settled change a user made goes into the history of the workhorse whose checkout holds the board, as one developer message, after the child, epoch, that workhorse's link and cursor are checked again. It starts no turn. Each delivery settles once as delivered, not delivered or unknown, and is never retried.

beats.heading: Each thread belongs to one tab session
beats.body: The tab sessions know which session owns each thread. A notification or tool call from a thread goes to that session alone, and an approval goes to the panes of that session (a workhorse's to those of its checkout), so one tab's news and approvals never reach another tab. A notification for a thread that no session owns yet goes to every session. A tool call from such a thread is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody.

beats.heading: A tab session ends 60 seconds after its last pane closes
beats.body: Every pane names its tab when its socket opens. When no pane of the tab comes back for 60 seconds, the session ends: its lease and link go, its pending approvals are cancelled, voice and board news stop, and each of its threads is unsubscribed once no turn runs on it, so Codex unloads it. A reload within that time keeps the conversation and its approvals. When the child exits, every session is dropped, and a tab's next message starts a new workhorse.

beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares an Archboard-only Codex home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. The owner lock and epoch ledger are the server's own. Then it starts the child and builds one generation's parts in the order they depend on each other.

beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: A tab holds one coordinator and a workhorse for each checkout
beats.body: Each browser tab is a tab session with its own lease and its own coordinator. A pane's first message or Talk starts its conversation: the coordinator first, then the workhorse of the checkout that pane shows, which that checkout's link then names. The pane that holds the lease sends its typed message straight to that workhorse as a turn or a steer, and edits that thread's queue. A pane that moves to another checkout reaches the workhorse there instead. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.heading: Voice is a separate thread that works in no checkout
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It runs in a directory of its own that holds no vault, so every command it runs names its checkout with -C. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorses and decides what the voice model says, and it runs only while voice is live. It does bounded work itself and routes anything sustained to the workhorse of the checkout it names, starting that workhorse when there is none. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The coordinator hears the workhorse at once
beats.body: While voice is live, a workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator, reaches the coordinator as one sentence in a turn/start: Codex adds it to the coordinator's running turn or starts one. With no voice session, or while a recording holds the voice, nothing is sent.

beats.heading: Board changes reach each workhorse quietly
beats.body: A settled change a user made goes into the history of the workhorse whose checkout holds the board, as one developer message, after the child, epoch, that workhorse's link and cursor are checked again. It starts no turn. Each delivery settles once as delivered, not delivered or unknown, and is never retried.

beats.heading: Each thread belongs to one tab session
beats.body: The tab sessions know which session owns each thread. A notification or tool call from a thread goes to that session alone, and an approval goes to the panes of that session (a workhorse's to those of its checkout), so one tab's news and approvals never reach another tab. A notification for a thread that no session owns yet goes to every session. A tool call from such a thread is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody.

beats.heading: A tab session ends 60 seconds after its last pane closes
beats.body: Every pane names its tab when its socket opens. When no pane of the tab comes back for 60 seconds, the session ends: its lease and link go, its pending approvals are cancelled, voice and board news stop, and each of its threads is unsubscribed once no turn runs on it, so Codex unloads it. A reload within that time keeps the conversation and its approvals. When the child exits, every session is dropped, and a tab's next message starts a new workhorse.
